title: NASA releases 360-degree view of Neretva Vallis from Perseverance rover
excerpt: The image was created using 217 individual photographs captured by the rover on May 20, 2024.
bodyHtml:
NASA released a new 360-degree panoramic view of Neretva Vallis within the Jezero Crater on October 26, 2026. The image was constructed from 217 separate photographs taken by the Mastcam-Z instrument on the Perseverance rover.

The data for this image was collected on May 20, 2024, which marked the 1,155th Martian day, or sol, of the mission. The agency provided an enhanced-color version of the vista, which was processed to improve visual contrast and highlight color differences in the terrain.

Operations for the Mastcam-Z instrument are led by Arizona State University in collaboration with Malin Space Science Systems and the Niels Bohr Institute of the University of Copenhagen. The Perseverance rover is managed by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory for NASA.
